title: The Linux clock reports a failure as -1, and the public header keeps the old return value

pr.title: Report a clock failure on Linux as -1
pr.description: On Linux, clock_uptime_ms() now returns -1 when the monotonic clock fails, so a caller can tell a failure from an uptime of 0. The CLI prints an error then. QueryPerformanceCounter never fails on Windows XP and later, so the Windows branch stays.

bugs.note: The doc comment of clock_uptime_ms in the public header include/clock.h still says that Linux returns 0 when the monotonic clock fails. The change returns -1 there, so a caller that follows the header checks for 0 and takes -1 as an uptime. The header line is unchanged code. Update the Linux line of the comment.

traps.why: %lld with a cast to long long prints an int64_t portably. A finding that it must use PRId64 or that the cast loses data is wrong.
